elements.quote: Systematic reviews of randomised controlled trials provide the strongest evidence to underpin healthcare decisions and can be used by guideline developers, such as the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE), to produce clinical guidelines that state treatment recommendations that health care providers follow to deliver patient care [1-5]. ... Nevertheless, Cochrane Reviews have been greatly under-utilised in guidelines and recommendations are often based on lowerlevel evidence or expert consensus because of limitations regarding familiarity, awareness, usefulness, access, and time [12-21]. ... There for two underlying assumptions of NMA: homogeneity, that also underlies PW-MA, and consistency [3, 29-32]. Unreliable results may be produced when either assumption is unreasonable [3, 24].
elements.reason: The Introduction describes the current state of knowledge (value of systematic reviews and Cochrane reviews, under‑utilisation in guidelines) and important uncertainties/limitations (limitations in use, NMA assumptions and potential for unreliable results).

elements.quote: Limited research has explored the use of NMAs to inform guidelines [38]. Lunny et al summarised how often NMAs and PW-MAs support recommendations in a sample of 50 guidelines [15]. Our article is the first to systematically search for reviews and summarise their citation in guidelines, and to explore the citation of reviews in depth. In this article, we build on prior research by conducting a systematic review of Cochrane Reviews that applied NMA to summarise which reviews were cited in guidelines in terms of review characteristics, when the reviews were cited, where the reviews were cited regarding location, who cited the reviews, and why the reviews were cited in terms of how the review contributed to the guideline.
elements.reason: The Introduction explains the gap (limited research on NMA use in guidelines), states novelty (first to systematically search and summarise citations), and the purpose/need for the current review.

elements.quote: Lunny et al summarised how often NMAs and PW-MAs support recommendations in a sample of 50 guidelines [15]. Our article is the first to systematically search for reviews and summarise their citation in guidelines, and to explore the citation of reviews in depth.
elements.reason: The Introduction cites prior similar work (Lunny et al) and explicitly states how the current review differs and the need for this updated/expanded systematic search.

No description is provided of the proposed mechanism(s) of action of interventions; the Introduction does not briefly describe how interventions included in the underlying Cochrane reviews are thought to work.
No logic model or mention of a hypothesised relationships diagram for complex interventions or delivery contexts is provided in the Introduction or elsewhere in the supplied evidence.

elements.quote: We aimed to summarise which, when, where, who, and why Cochrane Reviews that applied NMA were cited in guidelines; and to compare the citation of NMA reviews in guidelines with PW-MA reviews.
elements.reason: The abstract provides an explicit statement of the review objectives, clearly specifying the questions the review addresses (which/when/where/who/why NMA reviews were cited, and comparison with PW-MA reviews).

No explicit statement of planned comparisons using a PICO (or variant) for intervention effects is provided in the retrieved evidence; the manuscript describes inclusion of intervention reviews and extracted intervention details but does not present the planned comparisons framed as PICO.

elements.quote: We extracted the review citation, Cochrane Review Group, publication date, sources of support, types of studies and participants, the interventions in the network for the first outcome (i.e. the first outcome in the methods for which data were collected and NMA results were reported). For the first outcome, we extracted whether it was a primary or secondary outcome, the type of data, measure of effect used, the number of trials and patients analysed, whether heterogeneity or inconsistency were found and assessment methods, whether a frequentist or Bayesian approach was followed, grade ratings, and the risk of bias (for sequence generation and allocation concealment) of the studies included in the analysis.
elements.reason: The manuscript lists specific study characteristics and outcome-related details that were used to determine eligibility and for data extraction, including study types, participants, interventions, outcomes and analytic approaches.

elements.quote: Cochrane Reviews of interventions that applied NMA were included. We excluded protocols, withdrawn reviews, overview of reviews, and diagnostic test accuracy reviews.
elements.reason: The report specifies some report-level eligibility decisions (e.g. inclusion of Cochrane intervention reviews, exclusion of protocols and withdrawn reviews) and the search date is provided elsewhere, but it does not state language restrictions and gives limited detail on other report characteristics (e.g. dissemination year criteria beyond using publication date, or explicit publication/report status categories beyond those excluded).
No text in the provided evidence distinguishes excluding studies because outcomes were not measured versus excluding because outcome results were not reported.
The provided evidence does not specify the groups used in each synthesis or explicitly link synthesis groups to the comparisons defined in the review objectives.

elements.quote: We excluded reviews that used indirect comparison methods (e.g. calculating the difference between results obtained from pairwise meta-analyses) rather than NMA models because indirect comparisons are made in reviews without using searchable terminology. We excluded reviews that applied NMA but for which the main summary of findings table was based on PW-MA or single trials because we primarily aimed to explore the uptake of NMA results in clinical guidelines.
elements.reason: The manuscript provides rationales for notable eligibility restrictions (e.g. excluding indirect-comparison methods because they are not searchable, and excluding NMAs whose main summary relied on PW-MA or single trials because the aim was to study uptake of NMA results).

elements.quote: Continuous data were presented as medians and ranges, and numbers and percentages were displayed for categorical data. Histograms were used for the publication year, time to first citation, the number of times reviews were cited, and why reviews were cited. A map was used to present the location of guideline groups. A Kaplan Meier plot was presented for time to citation, which was calculated by subtracting the publication year of the review from the year that the review was first cited in a guideline. Reviews that were not cited were censored and their time to citation was calculated by subtracting the publication year of the review from the current year (2024). All figures were produced in Excel except Kaplan Meier plots which were constructed in R 4.4.0. Non-reported missing data were excluded from analyses.

elements.quote: Our findings are consistent with previous work. Korfitsen et al found that only 18% of 585 recommendations made in 56 guidelines published by the Danish Health Authority between 2014–2021, included evidence from a Cochrane Review [13]. Lunny et al found that 249 reviews (of which 64% were systematic reviews using PW-MAs and 3% using NMAs) were cited in 50 guidelines (dated 2017-2018) retrieved from the TRIP and Epistemonikos databases [15]. ... Previously, Vigna-Taglianti et al assessed the quality of 80 reviews cited in 128 guidelines regarding breast and colon cancer and found 70% of reviews were low quality reviews [17].
elements.reason: The discussion explicitly compares the study's findings with prior studies (Korfitsen et al., Lunny et al., Vigna-Taglianti et al.), interpreting results in the context of other relevant evidence.

elements.quote: Wefound that some guidelines cited low quality evidence and out-dated reviews. Of the 26 NMAreviews that were cited in guidelines, 50% reported heterogeneous results, 19% reported inconsistent results, 73% reported low and very low credibility results, and 15% included studies with a high risk of bias. If the findings were not suitably interpreted by the review authors or guideline developers, use of such reviews may lead to inappropriate recommendations. Furthermore, reviews require regular updating to include newly published studies or apply new methods that would alter findings [3].
elements.reason: The Discussion (Principal Findings) explicitly describes limitations of the included evidence: low quality/very low credibility, heterogeneity, inconsistency, high risk of bias, and that many reviews are out-dated, and notes potential impacts of these limitations on guideline recommendations.

No text in the retrieved evidence presents a discussion section that explicitly describes limitations of the review authors' own review processes (e.g. study selection, data extraction, analysis limitations). No retrieved text explicitly discusses the potential impact of each limitation of the review authors' review processes. While the Discussion addresses limitations of the included reviews (e.g. low quality, out-of-date) and possible impacts on guideline recommendations, it does not describe limitations of the review team's own processes nor the potential impact of those process limitations.

elements.quote: Improved collaboration and communication between review authors and guideline developers will help improve research efficiency by ensuring the research question is defined appropriately, informing guideline developers of a review's existence and findings, identifying whether there are areas for which a review is needed, facilitating knowledge exchange regarding specialist topics such as NMA, and avoiding un-necessary repetition of research.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly discusses practical implications and actions to improve uptake and use of NMA reviews in guidelines (e.g., improving collaboration and communication, informing guideline developers, facilitating knowledge exchange), addressing implications for practice.

elements.quote: As general guidance, the Cochrane recommends updating reviews at least every two years [3]. Yet, we found that 42% of cited NMA reviews were first cited between 2-6 years after publication, therefore guidelines may be citing out-dated reviews.
elements.reason: The paper notes implications relevant to guideline development and review-updating practice (mentioning Cochrane guidance and potential citation of outdated reviews) and discusses informing guideline developers, but it does not provide explicit, concrete policy recommendations (e.g., for health authorities or policymaking bodies) beyond general guidance and observations.
